pages.title: A obra e a situação

work.title: The Purple Cow
work.note: The Purple Cow é uma quadrinha humorística do escritor americano Gelett Burgess, publicada em 1895 na revista The Lark, de São Francisco. Em quatro versos curtos, o poeta diz que nunca viu uma vaca roxa e que não espera ver uma. O poema é leve, direto e brinca com um absurdo que parece óbvio. A referência mostra uma vaca de cor inesperada: light purple, dark purple.

pages.question: Como a história dessa obra ajuda você a imaginar a situação de hoje? Diga uma ideia em inglês.

compare.us: The US flag is red, white and blue. In English you say “mine is blue”: mine, yours, his, hers replace “my bag”, “your bag”.

pages.title: The red bag at the airport · 1/3
paragraphs: Lena is at the airport in **Phoenix**. She waits for her bag. Many bags come out on the belt. There are black bags, green bags and blue bags.
A young man points at a red bag. “**Excuse me, is this your bag?**” he asks. “No,” says Lena. “**Mine is blue**. This one is red.” Then she sees her bag. “Oh, **that’s mine**! Thank you!”
pages.prompt: Onde começa e o que acontece?

pages.title: The red bag at the airport · 2/3
paragraphs: The man smiles. “**What color is your phone?**” he asks. It is a strange question, but Lena answers: “It’s black. And yours?” “Mine is white,” he says. “**Nice colors!**”

Lena thinks of a funny poem called “The Purple Cow.” An American writer, Gelett Burgess, wrote it in 1895. He says he **never saw** a purple cow, and he never hopes to see one. “**That’s funny!**” Lena thinks. Her bag is not purple. It is a normal blue, but it is easy to find.

pages.title: The red bag at the airport · 3/3
paragraphs: The man takes the red bag. “**Not my color**,” he laughs, “but it is my bag!” Lena says goodbye. “**Take care of your things!**” she says. He smiles and waves.
